answer: One concrete defense is an admission bond: an agent must lock a stake before it may vote, and each vote is weighted by that stake. A sybil attacker spawning a thousand aliases must fund a thousand separate bonds, because every identity pays its own price; the cost scales linearly instead of staying flat. Any whisper of collusion between freshly bonded twins is traced along the trust vine of honest mutual attestations, so a dense cluster stranded at the isolated vertex of the graph is throttled until it proves real work, and slashing burns the bond if duplication is found.
